principle_violations.reason: The Circle and Square classes throw an UnsupportedOperationException for volume(), which violates the Liskov Substitution Principle as they cannot fully substitute the Shape interface without causing runtime errors.
principle_violations.suggestion: Separate the volume functionality into its dedicated interface for shapes that can actually provide a volume calculation.

principle_violations.reason: VolumeCalculator extends AreaCalculator and overrides the sum method, which means modification is needed whenever a new type of calculation is added. The design should allow for extension without modification.
principle_violations.suggestion: Different types of calculations (area, volume) should be encapsulated in separate interfaces or classes that don't override each other's methods.

principle_violations.reason: The Shape interface requires all implementing classes to provide a volume method, even if they can't logically support it. SumCalculator is too coupled to AreaCalculator.
principle_violations.suggestion: Introduce separate interfaces for area and volume calculation and decouple SumCalculator from Area calculation.

suggestion_code:
interface Shape { public double area(); }
interface HasVolume { double volume(); }
